description:
Every high achiever has a moment when blame stops working: a moment they stop pointing at the industry, the market, the parents, the ex, the ceiling, and start owning every part of their life. That moment is where extraordinary lives get built, and it is where this show goes.

The Honorée Corder Show is a long-form interview podcast hosted by Honorée Corder: bestselling author of 68 books, executive book producer, TEDx speaker, and founder of the Empire Builders Mastermind. Each week she sits down with a founder, author, executive, coach, attorney, or artist to trace the fork in the road they recognized, the choice they made to stop playing the victim, and what happened on the other side of that decision.

Guests include Wall Street Journal bestselling author Brittany Hodak, Real Artists Don't Starve author Jeff Goins, #1 Wall Street Journal bestselling ghostwriter Alice Sullivan, Cannes-winning voice actor Shelly Shenoy, Nashville K-9 founder Ali Hemyari, and more than a dozen other founders, coaches, and thought leaders across finance, real estate, marketing, hospitality, law, and executive coaching.

Expect honest conversation about entrepreneurship, leadership, mindset, personal accountability, writing and publishing, money, and the practice of taking full responsibility for your work and your life. No hustle-culture theater, and no credential stacking--just the decision that separates the people who build the life they want from the people who complain about the one they have.

Get a complimentary copy of Your Book Means Business here or at HonoreeCorder.com, and her Nonfiction Author's Empire Roadmap here.

93.3 WDRK is a fictional audio drama and a love letter to the small-town overnight radio shows of yesterday.


Every night, Tim settles behind the microphone to read community announcements, take calls from the people still awake, and keep the station company until morning.

Most callers just need someone to talk to. Others have stories they can’t explain and some seem to know more about the station than they should.


Set against the quiet back roads, dark woods, and isolated lakes of rural Arkansas, WDRK blends the familiar comfort of late-night radio with a slow-burning mystery unfolding one broadcast at a time.

The signal is clear. Somebody is always listening.

Keep the radio on.

Very Nonprofit – Very Real is the podcast about the people side of nonprofit leadership.


If you lead people in a nonprofit—whether you’re a supervisor, manager, director, or executive—you know this work is satisfying and, at times, incredibly challenging. Leading well isn’t just about programs and outcomes. It’s about people.


Hosted by nonprofit leader, educator, best-selling author, and coach, Paula MacLean, this podcast offers irresistibly useful insights you can take to work with you tomorrow. 


Each short, practical episode focuses on the real challenges nonprofit leaders face every day, including:

  •  having difficult conversations 
  •  supporting and retaining staff
  •  hiring for retention
  •  giving and receiving feedback 
  •  creating productive teams 
  •  navigating conflict
  •  successfully addressing performance issues 
  •  improving motivation and engagement 
  •  and many more to come! 


No theory. No fluff.  Just grounded, evidence-informed and experience-based guidance distilled from Paula's 40 year career working in and alongside nonprofits.


These episodes are designed to be shared, discussed, and used with your teams. Each one is a "mini-training" that will raise the bar of any leader at any level in your nonprofit. 


Whether you’re new to leadership or have been doing this work for years, you’ll find ideas, language, and approaches you can use immediately—with your team, in your organization, and in your day-to-day leadership.


Because in nonprofits, getting the people side of leadership right really matters!

title: "The Nine" Tapes

description:
In 1952, inside a secret laboratory in Maine, a doctor entered a trance and allegedly made contact with something calling itself “The Nine.” What began as a bizarre experiment would grow into a decades-long mystery. Throughout the 1970s and ’80s - and reportedly even today- different people around the world claimed to receive messages from the same mysterious intelligence. But what exactly were The Nine? Benevolent beings offering humanity a message? Something darker? A psychological phenomenon? Or was the entire story connected to experiments in mind control and manipulation?


The Nine Tapes investigates the strange history behind one of the most enduring - and little-known - mysteries of the paranormal, using a remarkable archive of original recordings, documents, and never-before-heard channeling tapes dating back to the 1950s. For the first time, we’ll hear the voices, follow the evidence, and attempt to answer a question that has remained unresolved for more than seventy years: Who - or what - are The Nine?

description:
The Modern Grooming Standard is a lifestyle and men's grooming podcast created for men who believe looking sharp should be simple, practical, and authentic. The series explores the everyday habits, hairstyling techniques, grooming routines, personal confidence, and style decisions that help men present their best selves without spending hours in front of the mirror.
Each episode takes a practical approach to modern grooming. Topics can range from choosing the right hair product and understanding the difference between pomade, clay, wax, paste, and gel to learning how to create professional hairstyles, maintain healthy-looking hair, build an efficient morning routine, and match a hairstyle with different occasions.
A central theme of the podcast is control without overdoing it. Modern men's hairstyles increasingly favor texture, movement, flexibility, and natural-looking finishes rather than excessively stiff or greasy styles. That philosophy aligns naturally with Shaar Official's Clay Pomade with Olive Oil, which is designed around strong yet flexible hold, a natural matte finish, lightweight application, and easy washout.
Throughout the series, listeners will also discover practical styling techniques, including how much product to use, how to warm styling products between the palms, how to distribute product through the hair, and how to build hold gradually rather than applying too much at once. For listeners interested in exploring a styling product built around this approach, click here ( https://shaarofficial.com/products/clay-pomade ) to learn more about Shaar's Clay Pomade with Olive Oil.
Podcast Objectives
------------------
The podcast will aim to:
* Educate men about modern hair styling and grooming.
* Explain the differences between popular men's hair products.
* Provide practical, easy-to-follow styling techniques.
* Help listeners select products according to hair length, desired hold, texture, and finish.
* Promote efficient grooming routines suitable for work, social occasions, and everyday life.
* Discuss the relationship between grooming, presentation, confidence, and personal style.
* Encourage listeners to achieve a polished appearance without making their hair look overly styled.
* Introduce Shaar Official naturally through relevant grooming conversations rather than aggressive product promotion.
Ideal Audience
--------------
The podcast is primarily designed for:
* Men interested in personal grooming.
* Professionals who want a clean, polished appearance.
* Men with short-to-medium hairstyles.
* Beginners learning how to use hair styling products.
* Men searching for matte-finish styling products.
* Fashion-conscious listeners interested in men's style.
* Anyone wanting a quicker and more effective daily grooming routine.
Suggested Episode Topics
------------------------
* Pomade vs. Clay: Which One Actually Fits Your Hairstyle?
* How to Get a Natural Matte Finish Without Making Hair Look Dry
* The Five Biggest Hair-Styling Mistakes Men Make
* How Much Hair Product Should You Actually Use?
* From Morning Routine to Boardroom: Building a Professional Grooming Routine
* Slick Back, Textured Crop, or Side Part: Choosing Your Signature Style
* Why Flexible Hold Is Changing Modern Men's Hairstyles
* Olive Oil, Argan Oil, and Shea Butter in Modern Hair Products
* How to Restyle Your Hair During a Busy Day
* Building Confidence Through Consistent Grooming

They were living civilizations of ambition, genius, cruelty, and hope — and their fall is the oldest lesson we have about the fragility of everything we build. Cinematic but accurate. title: We'll Talk About That
author: We'll Talk About That
description:
What started out as a shared love for Dance and Reality TV has now evolved into We’ll Talk About That. Hosted by friends Matthew and Camille, this podcast creates a space that explores topics beyond what first brought us together, now allowing us to talk more about our respective experiences, interests and stages of life. title: Founder of Peace
author: Matthew Braidley
description: Founder of Peace is a podcast about finding real peace in a peaceless world through Jesus Christ. Hosted by Matthew Braidley—entrepreneur, pianist, husband, and father of five—each episode features honest conversations about faith, struggle, redemption, and the pursuit of a Christ-centered life. Through powerful stories and reflections, discover how true peace is not found in the world, but in the Savior who overcame it.

title: The GinaCology Podcast
author: Gina Cloud
description:
The GinaCology Podcast with Gina Cloud is a deep exploration into the evolution and the revolution of the ideas that have defined and confined women across biology, culture, sexuality, spirituality and personal identity. This is a space devoted to reclaiming the feminine in her full expression: powerful, wise, sensual, cyclical, and deeply embodied.
Through the lens of ancient feminine wisdom and modern lived experience, each episode invites you back into relationship with your body as your greatest guide—your internal GPS (G.oddess P.ower S.ource). Through the portals found in our biological life cycles: Menstruation, Pregnancy and Menopause, this podcast challenges what you’ve been taught and opens the door to helping you remember what you already know. For more info, and to join my list, come find me at ginacloud.com, on Instagram @ginacloud, and on TikTok @ginacloudginacology. Awaken to your power... I'm calling to you.

title: The Oncology Minute

title: 90% of the Job: Surviving Auditions as a Working Actor
author: Avery Whitted
description:
Most of the life of an actor is not spent on stage or in front of a camera. It's spent scrolling through casting notices, memorizing lines, uploading self-tapes, juggling day jobs, and waiting for something to click. 
It's hard out here! But you don't have to go it alone. Join us for conversations with professional actors, stories, questions, advice, insight, and much more. 
Every episode we work to demystify the grind, and make each audition a little bit easier. 
Hosted by fellow working actor Avery Whitted.

title: Life, Courage, Chaos, & Cuss Words
author: Ashley Golden
description:
Real life doesn't come tied in a neat little bow. Life, Courage, Chaos & Cuss Words is the uncensored therapy couch for anyone surviving the messy reality behind closed doors. ​
Hosted by a mom of seven navigating ADHD, adoption, a 24-year Army spouse life, and the pitch-black humor that comes from years investigating child abuse and neglect. This isn’t parenting advice or military PR—it’s honest storytelling, unfiltered rants, and laughing so you don’t lose your mind.

title: The Rooted Home
author: Jeremy & Lauren Mefford
description:
The Rooted Home is a faith-centered podcast for families who want to build intentional, fruitful homes that are rooted in scripture. Join husband and wife co-hosts Jeremy and Lauren Mefford for honest, biblical conversations about faith, family, and the rhythms of home life.

Each episode, we talk about what matters most in the home: biblical wisdom for everyday life, practical homemaking and family systems, rhythms that honor God without burning anyone out, and the kind of intentional, present family life the world isn't selling you. We'll talk about marriage, parenting, homeschooling, countering cultural pressure, and the beauty of choosing a slower, Christ-centered way of living together.

Subscribe wherever you listen--and join us every other week in our living room!

title: Filmmaker Spotlight
author: Warren Workman
description: Filmmaker Spotlight is where filmmakers talk honestly about the work behind the work. Host Warren Workman sits down with directors, producers, writers, actors, and other independent filmmakers to discuss how their projects came together, what they learned along the way, and what it really takes to keep creating. description:
D10tion Gaming: Ashkeepers Legacy is a cinematic Dungeons & Dragons Actual Play where found family, impossible choices, bad decisions, and the occasional very unlucky dice roll collide.


New to the story? You’re in the right place.


The podcast begins with a special series of Act 1 recap episodes, bringing you into the world, introducing the characters, unpacking the moments that shaped them, and giving you everything you need to know before the next chapter begins. Game Master Dominick Dawson sits down with the cast and crew to revisit the story so far, the choices that changed everything, and where each character stands heading into Act 2.

description:
The Sacred Listening podcast is a sanctuary for those who feel overwhelmed, overscheduled, and overbusy. In this podcast, we explore the various paths of restoring balance in our body from issues such as depletion, anxiety, chronic pain, and stress. We do this by redefining what self-care means on an individual level as we dive into cutting-edge research, personal stories, expert interviews, as well as listening in to the magic and mysticism of our body's wisdom. I welcome you to join us to reclaim self-agency over your health and wellbeing.
Elaine Oyang is an IAYT-certified yoga therapist and a self-nurture advocate. Throughout her 12+ year of teaching yoga in studios and private practice, she works to help others restore balance in their bodies from their over-busy lives. She's worked many years in private practice to help clients through their journeys of chronic pain, chronic illness, anxiety, insomnia, and loss of sense of self. With her podcast, Sacred Listening, Elaine shares with a wider audience on her personal experience, and that of her clients', on how to reclaim self-care and self-love.

description:
Better Medicine with Dr. Var is a science-grounded health podcast that brings together conventional, functional, integrative, lifestyle, and obesity medicine to help you understand why your body feels off — and what actually helps.
Hosted by Dr. Var, a triple board-certified physician(Family, Obesity, Lifestyle Medicine) with advanced training in functional and integrative medicine, this podcast is for people who are tired of being told “your labs are normal” while they still feel exhausted, inflamed, foggy, or stuck.
Each episode breaks down complex health topics — hormones, metabolism, gut health, inflammation, brain health, weight resistance, and longevity — into clear, practical insights you can use to have better conversations with your healthcare provider and make informed choices about your health.
This is not about rejecting medicine.
It’s about doing medicine better — by addressing root causes, honoring individual biology, and treating the whole person instead of just managing symptoms.
Educational only. Always work with your healthcare provider.

title: The Sound of the Altar

description: The Sound of the Altar with Vania Costner is a prophetic teaching podcast for Kingdom artisans, intercessors, worshipers, and scribes who desire to hear and carry what Heaven is saying. Through teachings on worship, intercession, Kingdom artistry, prophetic sound, and the ministry of the scribe, each series explores how the Father forms the vessel before releasing the assignment. I'm your host, Rickard Malmsten.

Join us each week to find beauty in the little things and strength in life’s challenges.

title: Exploited
author: Paulosophia Productions - Paul Martin
description:
Every one of these deaths is a transaction. Somebody got paid.


Exploited is a series about the intersection of addiction and organized crime — a global illicit drug trade worth hundreds of billions of dollars a year, built on a core relationship between those who can't simply quit and those who don't want them to.


Two forces meet here. One lives in the shadowy world of greed, crime, power, and corruption: the cartels, the chemists, the dealers in the phone, the industries that learned the same trick. The exploiters. The other navigates family trauma, poverty, peer pressure, the digital age, and the pull of a drug that rewrites the brain. The exploited.


Host Paul Martin, founder of United Against Fentanyl, sits down with insiders who understand both — people in recovery and people who have buried their children, and the agents, scientists, reporters, and former players who know how the machine runs. Raw testimonies. Hidden realities. Fentanyl is where it starts. It is not where it stops.

title: Meridian Silt
author: SLEUTH SYNDICATE
description:
Every river has a bottom. A place where the current slows down, and everything the water carries finally drops. In the deep South, they call it silt. It turns the water thick and brown. It buries things.
On February 26, 2014, twenty-one-year-old towboat worker Christian Andreacchio walked off his shift and into a storm. Hours later, he was found dead in the bathroom of his Meridian, Mississippi apartment. Within forty-five minutes of arriving on the scene, local police stamped the official file: suicide. Case closed.
But physics, forensics, and time refuse to cooperate with the official narrative. Meridian Silt goes past the badge to look at what happens when the mechanisms of justice freeze in place to protect a mistake. This isn't just a whodunit—it’s an exposé on the bureaucratic shell game, the suppression of grand jury evidence, and the terrifying legal brick walls that force grieving families to become their own detectives.
When the system protects itself instead of the victim... who keeps watch over the soil? Subscribe to Meridian Silt.
*Disclaimer:* Meridian Silt is an investigative podcast intended for educational and informational purposes. The views, hypotheses, and conclusions expressed by the host and independent forensic experts are based strictly on public records, sworn depositions, and independent investigative reviews. The events and individuals discussed are evaluated under a framework of ongoing public interest and systemic critique. All individuals mentioned are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law.

title: My Invisible Disease
author: Jenny Nicoll and Kassy Draper
description: The mental, the emotional, and the spiritual side of living with chronic illness and invisible disease. Hosts, Jenny Nicoll and Kassy Draper, longtime friends and young moms share their experience while in the trenches with symptoms and side effects of chronic illness. Jenny’s wait for transplant and Kassy’s journey to diagnosis inspired the podcast where they interview guests and discuss hacks to keep their heads above water. They see you, and your own struggle with your own invisible disease. And the challenges of balancing motherhood, managing a household, family, and career! Not all days are good and sometimes you don’t make it out of bed, or struggle to make it through the week. With a focus on mindset and a positive perspective, they strive to create a community where mamas can come together and be seen for more than their invisible disease.

title: SEEING JOHNNY ROKKETS
author: Dead Ahead Books
description:
The Zombie Apocalypse isn't the hardest part of growing up—it's keeping your little sister from hugging your undead father. Sixteen-year-old Sarah Burrows is the reluctant caretaker of her younger sister, Misty, and four troubled kids left behind at the Peaceful Acres Psychiatric Center for Obsessive Behavior. Her ragtag crew of survivors includes Jordan, a self-proclaimed psychic; Barton, a pudgy karate enthusiast; Alvin, a logical genius; and Zach, an unrelenting pessimist.
When Misty's grief reaches a breaking point, she demands to travel to Memphis to meet Johnny Rokkets—a legendary rock star who supposedly died in 1997, but who their father always claimed secretly lived upstairs in his Rokkland mansion. Knowing that staying hidden means losing Misty to her own delusions, Sarah realizes the only way to save her sister is to actually hit the road.
Armed with fake psychic visions, martial arts bravado, and a large pickle jar carrying a severed zombie hand, these kids must navigate a wasteland of walking corpses, explosive booby traps, and heavily armed survivalist camps. Will they find a dead legend hiding upstairs in Memphis, or will the harsh reality of the apocalypse finally catch up to them? Buckle up for a heavy-metal road trip fueled by hope, stolen machinery, and the healing power of rock and roll.

It’s been more than a year since the Eaton and Palisades Fires. And since then, Southern California Edison has focused on recovery initiatives including the launch of a new one-stop resource center designed to help Altadena community members navigate the rebuild and recovery process.
 
To hear more about SCE’s commitment to help communities recover and rebuild, host Audrey Ngo speaks with Edison International president & CEO Pedro Pizarro, SCE executive vice president and COO Jill Anderson and Kenneth Feinberg and Camille Biros, who designed the Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program.
 
They’ll discuss how SCE is supporting the Altadena and Malibu communities’ recovery and rebuilding efforts, the community’s role in shaping the Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program, steps SCE is taking to strengthen its wildfire mitigation approach and the launch of the Altadena Rebuild and Community Hub.
 
GUESTS:
Pedro Pizarro, Edison International president & CEO
Jill Anderson, SCE executive vice president and COO
Kenneth R. Feinberg and Camille S. Biros, Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program Designers

With nearly 70 years of combined expertise in psychiatry, Docs Tracey and Paul are dedicated to fostering a compassionate dialogue surrounding mental health, ultimately advocating for the dignity and respect of those affected by mental illness.
**DISCLAIMER: This podcast discusses mental health topics that may be sensitive or triggering for some listeners. The information shared is for educational and general discussion purposes only, and is not a substitute for personalized medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Please consult your own qualified healthcare professional for guidance tailored to your unique needs and circumstances. 
If you are in crisis, reach out to a local mental health provider or call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988.

description:
Becoming Set Apart is about breaking free from what keeps us bound—addiction, destructive habits, unhealthy patterns, our past, society’s expectations, and other people’s definitions of who we’re supposed to be—and becoming who God made and called us to be.
Hosted by Kentrell, also known as Set Apart, this isn’t a podcast from somebody standing at the finish line telling everybody else how to get there. He’s still becoming too.
Through honest conversations, personal testimony, practical challenges, and faith, Becoming Set Apart explores what real change looks like when life is still messy. Some episodes go deep into recovery and the things we use to escape. Others deal with discipline, physical fitness, relationships, identity, purpose, Scripture, and the everyday work required to become different—not just talk about being different.
The show is built around three pillars: Recovery. Fitness. Faith.
Recovery is bigger than sobriety. It means confronting whatever has control over you, understanding what’s underneath it, and learning how to stop running back to the same things that keep you stuck.
Fitness is about stewardship and discipline—learning to take care of the body you’ve been given and discovering how physical growth can strengthen the way you approach the rest of your life.
Faith is the foundation underneath it all. Not performative Christianity. Not pretending believers never struggle. Faith that gets tested in real life, in weakness, failure, temptation, grief, uncertainty, and the decision to keep following God when becoming who He called you to be is uncomfortable.
This is Faith for the Flawed.
For the person recovering.
For the person rebuilding.
For the person who believes in God but still struggles.
For the person who knows something has to change.
And for anybody learning that being set apart isn't something you suddenly arrive at.
It’s something you become.

A ottocento anni dalla morte di San Francesco, Luna Esposito e fra Roberto Pasolini partono dalla sua vita per parlare, in realtà, di noi: di fragilità, relazioni, fraternità, potere, accoglienza, limite e morte. Quattro conversazioni per riscoprire la piccolezza non come rinuncia o sconfitta, ma come possibilità di stare al mondo senza doverne essere sempre il centro.

title: The Sovereign Friend with KC
author: KC
description:
Hey friend, and welcome.
Have you ever wondered what it would feel like to walk beside God the way you’d walk beside someone who already knows you, already loves you, and already wants good for you? Not a distant God up in the clouds somewhere, watching from far away — but a Friend who walks right next to you, through every season, every valley, every green pasture.
That’s what The Sovereign Friend is all about.
I’m KC, and each episode, we open up Scripture together — slowly, honestly, and with a whole lot of heart. We dig into the stories, the original Hebrew and Greek words, and the deep, beautiful truths tucked inside God’s Word — not to make you feel like you need a theology degree to keep up, but to help you fall in love with the God who has been pursuing you all along.
This isn’t a rushed, surface-level Bible study. It’s a slow walk through Scripture with someone who wants to sit in the wonder right alongside you — the kind of conversation you’d have with a good friend by a quiet stream, sun on your face, nothing to prove and nowhere to rush off to.
Whether you’re just beginning to explore faith, coming back to God after time away, or you’ve walked with Him for years and just want to go deeper — there’s a place for you here. Come as you are. Bring your questions, your doubts, your joy, your tired heart. God already knows all of it, and He’s already glad you’re here.
Because Scripture doesn’t just inform the mind — it leads the heart home to God.
”That they may build me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them.” — Exodus 25:8 (KJV)
